content: The ATP-binding cassette sub-family A member 7 (ABCA7) is a protein encoded by the ABCA7 gene in humans. This protein belongs to the ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporter superfamily, which is responsible for transporting various molecules across both extracellular and intracellular membranes. ABC transporters are categorized into seven distinct subfamilies: ABC1, MDR/TAP, CFTR/MRP, ALD (adrenoleukodystrophy), OABP, GCN20, and White. ABCA7 is specifically a member of the ABC1 subfamily, which is unique in that it is exclusively found in multicellular eukaryotic organisms. The ABCA7 protein is classified as a full transporter and is predominantly expressed in myelo-lymphatic tissues. The highest levels of expression have been observed in peripheral leukocytes, the thymus, the spleen, and the bone marrow. Although the precise function of ABCA7 remains unclear, its expression pattern strongly suggests that it plays a role in regulating lipid homeostasis within immune system cells. Additionally, alternative splicing of the ABCA7 gene results in the production of two distinct transcript variants. From a clinical perspective, variants of the ABCA7 gene that disrupt the function of the protein have been associated with an increased risk of developing Alzheimer’s disease. Data from the Icelandic database of Decode Genetics has demonstrated that individuals with inactive variants of the ABCA7 gene have approximately double the likelihood of developing Alzheimer’s disease compared to those without such variants.
